title: [EXCLUDED] Permanent of a random symmetric Rademacher matrix is n^{(1/2-o(1))n}
statement: Conjecture 6.11. With probability 1 - o(1), |Per M_n^sym| = n^{(1/2-o(1))n}.
resolved_by: Kwan and Sauermann, 'On the permanent of a random symmetric matrix' (arXiv 2010.08922; Selecta Math. 2022). Source: 'Conjecture 6.11. With probability 1-o(1), |Per M_n^sym| = n^{(1/2-o(1))n}' for the symmetric matrix with i.i.d. Rademacher entries on and above the diagonal. Paper's abstract: 'the permanent of M_n has magnitude n^{n/2+o(n)} with probability 1-o(1)', for the random symmetric n x n matrix whose entries are independent Rademacher random variables, 'resolving a conjecture of Vu'. Same object, same statement.

title: [EXCLUDED] Limiting distribution of the second eigenvalue of a random regular graph
locator: Section 7, PDF p. 12 ('the real question ... is to compute the limiting distribution of lambda(G_{n,d})')
statement: 'While showing the existence of Ramanujan graphs is already highly non-trivial, the real question, in our opinion, is to compute the limiting distribution of lambda(G_{n,d}), which would lead to the exact probability of a random regular graph being Ramanujan.'
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08; also duplicates the Codex-tree row C0136 (pete_pgg_notes, Conjecture 7.15, Tracy-Widom fluctuations of the second eigenvalue of random regular graphs).
resolved_by: Huang, McKenzie and Yau, 'Ramanujan property and edge universality of random regular graphs' (arXiv 2412.20263, 2024): for fixed d >= 3 the extreme eigenvalues of the random d-regular graph have Tracy-Widom_1 fluctuations, hence a random d-regular graph is Ramanujan with probability tending to about 69 percent. Source asks for the limiting distribution of lambda(G_{n,d}); the paper's abstract states the limiting (Tracy-Widom) distribution of the second eigenvalue and the resulting Ramanujan probability. Recorded here also because the campaign already holds the problem as C0136.

title: [EXCLUDED] Delocalisation of two-dimensional interfaces with the hammock potential
statement: Open Problem 2. Prove delocalization in low dimensions for a larger class of interactions than those treated in [Brascamp-Lieb-Lebowitz] and [Ioffe-Shlosman-Velenik]. For example, the interesting case of the Hammock potential, V(x) = 0 for |x| < 1 and V(x) = infinity for |x| > 1, is still open.
resolved_by: Milos and Peled, 'Delocalization of two-dimensional random surfaces with hard-core constraints' (Comm. Math. Phys. 340 (2015) 1-46, arXiv 1404.5895). Source's example: the hammock potential in low dimension. Paper's abstract: random surfaces on a two-dimensional torus with a nearest-neighbour potential that is C^2 on an interval and infinite outside, 'no convexity assumption is made and the case of the so-called hammock potential is included'; main result: 'these surfaces delocalize, having fluctuations whose variance is at least of order log n'. The general 'larger class' part of the problem is programmatic and not admitted separately; the named example is settled.

title: [EXCLUDED] Talagrand's convexity conjecture (creating convexity in a bounded number of Minkowski sums)
locator: Conjecture 2.1, Section 2, PDF p. 1 (also talagrand_convexity_2013, prize note)
statement: Conjecture 2.1. There exists epsilon > 0 and an integer q with the following property. For any M, and any compact balanced set A in R^M with gamma(A) >= 1 - epsilon, we can find a convex compact set B contained in A + ... + A (q times) with gamma(B) >= 1/2.
resolved_by: Hua, Song and Tudose, 'On Talagrand's Convexity Conjecture' (arXiv 2605.10908, May 2026): 'any random vector in R^n which is dominated in convex order by a standard Gaussian vector can be written as the sum of three standard Gaussian vectors ... It also solves M. Talagrand's convexity problem, which in turn implies a weak version of a combinatorial analogue to the problem.' An earlier preprint (arXiv 2502.10382) claims the same conclusion via 'sum of a universal number of Gaussian vectors'. Source's Conjecture 2.1 is the convexity problem the abstract names. The combinatorial analogue (Conjecture 7.1) is NOT covered (only a weak version) and is admitted as F0057.

title: [EXCLUDED] The Bernoulli conjecture
locator: Conjecture 5.4, Section 5, PDF p. 4 (also talagrand_prizes_2016, Section 2)
statement: Conjecture 5.4 (The Bernoulli Conjecture). There exists a universal constant L such that given any finite set S and any set T of sequences indexed by S, we can find two sets of sequences T_1 and T_2 with, for M = b(T): sum_i |t_i| <= L M for all t in T_1; E sup_{t in T_2} |sum_i g_i t_i| <= L M; and T contained in T_1 + T_2.
status_search: Known result; the prize page (talagrand_prizes_2016, 2012 text) still lists it, the 2016 STOC paper predates the solution.
resolved_by: Bednorz and Latala, 'On the boundedness of Bernoulli processes' (Ann. of Math. 180 (2014) 1167-1203): they prove exactly the decomposition T subset T_1 + T_2 with the l^1 and Gaussian bounds, i.e. Talagrand's Bernoulli conjecture, for which Talagrand paid the prize. Same statement.

title: [EXCLUDED] Talagrand's selector process conjecture
statement: Conjecture 5.7. There exists a number L with the following property. Consider any 0 < p < 1, any set S and any set T of sequences (t_i)_{i in S} with t_i >= 0, and E_p(T) := E_p sup_{t in T} sum_{i in X} t_i. Then the class {X : sup_{t in T} sum_{i in X} t_i >= L E_p(T)} is p-small. (Conjectures 5.2/5.3 are the equivalent covering form: Psi(A) <= L E_p(A).)
resolved_by: Park and Pham, 'On a conjecture of Talagrand on selector processes and a consequence on positive empirical processes' (Ann. of Math. 199 (2024) 1293-1321, arXiv 2204.10309): 'we prove a conjecture of Talagrand that is the analog of Talagrand's Gaussian processes result in the Bernoulli-p setting', i.e. the selector process conjecture; a sharp version is in arXiv 2412.03540. The source's Conjecture 5.7 is that selector-process statement (E_p(T) is bounded only through explicit p-small witnesses).

title: [EXCLUDED] The Kahn-Kalai conjecture in Talagrand's form
statement: Conjecture 8.1 [Kahn-Kalai]. There exists a universal constant L such that for all 0 < p < 1 if A in {0,1}^S is an up-class that satisfies mu_p(A) <= 1/2, then A is p'-small for p' = p/(L log card S).
resolved_by: Park and Pham, 'A proof of the Kahn-Kalai conjecture' (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), arXiv 2203.17207): the threshold p_c(F) of an increasing property is at most K q(F) log l(F), where q(F) is the expectation threshold defined by exactly Talagrand's p-small covers. Same statement up to the choice of the logarithm's argument (log card S versus log of the maximal minimal element), which Talagrand notes is immaterial. Conjecture 8.3 (the fractional version with a delta-spread measure) is the Frankston-Kahn-Narayanan-Park theorem (Ann. of Math. 194 (2021)).

title: [EXCLUDED] Pfaffian structure of the branching-coalescing point set of the Brownian net
statement: (1) Is the Brownian net integrable in the sense that the branching-coalescing point set defined in (3.10) admits an explicit characterization, similar to the Pfaffian point process characterization of the coalescing point set discussed in Remark 2.10?
resolved_by: Garrod, Tribe and Zaboronski, 'Examples of interacting particle systems on Z as Pfaffian point processes: coalescing-branching random walks and annihilating random walks with immigration' (Ann. Henri Poincare 21 (2020), arXiv 1605.09668): the abstract states that coalescing and branching random walks on Z are Pfaffian point processes at fixed times for all deterministic initial conditions, and that 'various limiting Pfaffian point processes on R [are] found by diffusive rescaling, including the point set process for the Brownian net'. That is the explicit characterization the source asks for.

title: [EXCLUDED] Construction of the Levy (stable) web in the paths topology
statement: (5) ... Can one construct the Levy web in the paths topology, and what type of special points may arise? ... Identifying [the density constant] C would allow one to determine the sharp asymptotic rate of decay for the density of coalescing random walks on Z in the domain of attraction of a stable Levy process.
resolved_by: Mountford, Ravishankar and Valle, 'A construction of the stable web' (arXiv 1803.06739, ALEA 2019) construct 'a process on the space of coalescing cadlag stable paths' and prove convergence of coalescing stable random walks to it; 'Construction and convergence results for stable webs' (arXiv 2106.02944, SPA 2024) gives a metric on aged paths and tightness/convergence for 1 < alpha <= 2. The construction half of the question is therefore done; the special-points classification and the density constant C are not addressed by these abstracts and are left as a note rather than admitted separately, since the source poses them as sub-parts of the construction question.

title: [EXCLUDED] Hamiltonicity threshold of a random subgraph of the hypercube
statement: Determine the threshold for a random subgraph of the n-cube to be Hamiltonian.
resolved_by: Condon, Espuny Diaz, Girao, Kuhn and Osthus, 'Hamiltonicity of random subgraphs of the hypercube' (Mem. Amer. Math. Soc. 2024, arXiv 2007.02891): for the random subgraph of Q^n with edge probability p > 1/2 (and the hitting-time version at minimum degree 2), the subgraph is Hamiltonian whp; the threshold is p = 1/2, settling the question as stated.

title: [EXCLUDED] Non-singularity of random symmetric 0-1 matrices with r ones per row and column
statement: Let M be randomly chosen from the set of n x n symmetric {0,1} matrices with r >= 3 ones in each row and column. Prove that M is non-singular w.h.p.
resolved_by: Huang, 'Invertibility of adjacency matrices for random d-regular graphs' (Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), arXiv 1807.06465): the adjacency matrix of the random d-regular graph, d >= 3 fixed, is non-singular with probability 1 - n^{-c}; Meszaros (2020) independently for fixed d. The source's matrix (symmetric 0-1, r ones per row/column, zero diagonal implicit) is the adjacency matrix of a random r-regular graph. The sharp singularity exponent remains open and is admitted as F0003.

title: [EXCLUDED] One-endedness of wired minimal spanning forest trees and the Timar theorem; scaling limit of the planar MST
locator: Question 6.7, PDF p. 26 and Question 6.14, PDF p. 27
statement: Question 6.7. If G is a unimodular transitive graph and WMSF != FMSF, does FMSF-a.s. every tree have infinitely many ends? Question 6.14. One may consider the minimal spanning tree on epsilon Z^2 in R^2 and let epsilon -> 0. It would be interesting to show that the limit exists in various senses.
status_search: The source itself records Timar's proof for 6.7; WebSearch 2026-09-08 for 6.14.
resolved_by: 6.7: Timar, 'Ends in free minimal spanning forests' (Ann. Probab. 34 (2006)), as the source states ('a proof of this conjecture was obtained by Timar'). 6.14: Garban, Pete and Schramm, 'The scaling limits of the minimal spanning tree and invasion percolation in the plane' (Ann. Probab. 46 (2018)): existence and uniqueness of the scaling limit of the MST on the triangular lattice (and invariance under rotations/scalings) in the sense of the quad-crossing/tree topology; the source asks for existence of the limit 'in various senses'. The remaining LPS questions (6.5, 6.6, 6.8-6.13) coincide with Lyons-Peres book Questions 11.x already in the campaign (P0055-P0062) and are not re-admitted.

title: [EXCLUDED] Hausdorff dimension of the SLE_kappa hull boundary and reversibility of SLE
locator: Section 11.2, PDF p. 92 (boundary dimension) and Section 11.2.3 (reversibility)
statement: Prove that the Hausdorff dimension of the boundary of K_t is almost surely 1 + 2/kappa when K_t is the hull of an SLE_kappa (chordal or radial) for kappa > 4. [11.2.3:] the conjecture that chordal SLE_kappa is reversible.
resolved_by: Boundary dimension: SLE duality (Zhan, 'Duality of chordal SLE', Invent. Math. 174 (2008); Dubedat, 'Duality of Schramm-Loewner evolutions', Ann. Sci. ENS 2009) identifies the hull boundary with an SLE_{16/kappa}-type curve, whose dimension 1 + 2/kappa follows from Beffara's dimension theorem, exactly the route the source anticipates. Reversibility: Zhan, 'Reversibility of chordal SLE' (Ann. Probab. 36 (2008)) for kappa <= 4; Miller and Sheffield, 'Imaginary geometry III' (Ann. of Math. 184 (2016)) for 4 < kappa <= 8; and reversibility fails for kappa > 8 (Rohde-Schramm), so the conjecture is settled in every case. The source's other open items (conformal invariance of the self-avoiding walk, critical random-cluster interfaces, theta(p_c) = 0 in three dimensions) are already in the campaign (D0066, C0049/P0124, grimmett_2022 rows) and are not re-admitted.

title: [EXCLUDED] Kerov's conjecture on Macdonald-positive specializations
statement: Conjecture 7.6 (Kerov). The Macdonald-positive specializations are parameterized by pairs of sequences of non-negative reals alpha, beta with sum (alpha_i + beta_i) < infinity and an additional parameter gamma >= 0 (the explicit list of the source).
resolved_by: Matveev, 'Macdonald-positive specializations of the algebra of symmetric functions: proof of the Kerov conjecture' (Ann. of Math. 189 (2019) 277-316): proves that every Macdonald-positive specialization is of the listed form, which is 'the completeness of the list given in Conjecture 7.6' that the source calls a hard open problem.

title: [EXCLUDED] Aging for the REM under Metropolis dynamics
locator: Section 6, 'Open questions and conjectures', PDF p. 45
statement: 'It would be nice to replace the RHT dynamics by a more physical dynamics, like e.g. Glauber, or, at least, to explore the a != 0 case. We believe that the long-time behaviour of the model should not change dramatically, however we do not know any proof of it.'
resolved_by: Gayrard, 'Aging in Metropolis dynamics of the REM: a proof' (Probab. Theory Related Fields 174 (2019) 501-551, arXiv 1602.06081): proves the arcsine aging law for the Metropolis dynamics of the random energy model, i.e. the 'more physical dynamics' the source asks for; earlier, Mathieu-Mourrat and Gayrard treated the a != 0 (asymmetric) trap dynamics. Not admitted.
